label: third original token when the second original token is n
explanation: Fires only at step t=2 (the third original input) when the token before it (original token 1) is n. On dev, every active step satisfies this and every such step is active (P=R=F1=1.0). The current input token, L and the digit count barely change the firing rate. It never fires at other original positions after an n, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Magnitude depends on context: all the top activations (about 0.80) are sequences starting u n, and the low-quartile examples start k n, d n or l n, so the first token seems to scale the strength. That is only from the examples; I did not measure it systematically.

issues: None of the checks found a systematic problem. Test split: P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0 (16689 active steps, all predicted), and the coverage in every activation quartile is 1.0. Running misses with --split test gives 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The profile backs up the factual claims: all activations are at t=2 (orig_idx 2), and the delimiter and copy phase have 0 activations. The firing rate by in_tok is flat (about 0.003 for every token). The by-L rates differ only because each length contributes a different number of steps; the active counts per L are about the same.

The magnitude claim is only weakly checked. The top examples are all 'u n X' at about 0.80 and a low-quartile example is 'k n w' at 0.07, which fits first-token-dependent scaling. Correlation of the binary predicate with activation is 0.926, so magnitude does vary. The agent correctly said this was anecdotal. It sits in the explanation, not the label, so it does not count against upholding.
